entry.text: Another day, another victory in our heroic struggle against health campaigns and self-control.
And to celebrate the triumph - give me a tin of Morley and papers.

options.text: Someone left me a tooth last shift

response.text: Charming. Even tied up with a bow.

options.text: What's that thing by the till?

response.text: Ah, right. There's a human tooth in it.
Let's say it's... something somebody left, to pass on to someone else... only nobody's, you know, a hundred percent sure who.
Can't say more, but if you feel like playing dental Cinderella, go ahead.
Don't even start.

options.text: What was it you asked for?

wrong_items.text: God... Alright, let's go slow. See that red-and-white tin on the shelf, says Morley? Yes, that's tobacco. Good.
Now, on the counter, your left hand, the greenish box with papers in it. Open it. Take exactly one pack. That's it.

options.text: Should I just offer it to everyone?

response.text: Oh, like you're brave enough for that.
...From what I gathered, if you can't slip it in quietly, better not. No need to make things weirder.
Talk to people, play some mind games. Drop the jar in with their order if you're sure enough.
Just know they might notice it the moment they leave, tomorrow, or never. And if you've backed the wrong horse, there's no guarantee you'll ever see the thing again.
[Saved to ⚙ Help.]

options.text: You know anyone missing a tooth?

response.text: Ha. In Larris? Could be half the town.
But it doesn't look ancient. Someone probably dropped it fairly recently.

options.text: Got any idea how I could slip it to someone?

response.text: Hm. Ehhh... jeepers.
I suppose I'd just sneak the jar into their order and hope for the best.
Of course, they may notice it the moment they leave, tomorrow, or never. And if you've backed the wrong horse, there's no guarantee you'll ever see the thing again.
After that, it's all luck. You place your little wager, the town decides whether you've won.
[Saved to ⚙ Help.]

checkout.text: Thanks. Have fun with your cancer sticks and human leftovers.

check.text: And good work with the till. Did it neater than me. Keep it up, that's yours to handle at the end of every shift now.

check_irresponsible3.text: And the till... Thought I asked you to count it last shift. Maybe I forgot, maybe you slacked off. Either way, do it today. End of every shift, it's your job.

bye.text: Alright, I'm off to greater things.

entry.text: Good morning, and may your day be as bright as your smile and as lovely as your heart.
Blessed morning, sweet face. We're here for cigarettes, but decided to be a little poetic about it today.
What lulls from a drawer and eases your blues, holds the colour of veins and a yesterday bruise?

click.text: ...What about smoking it behind the pharmacy again? No one ever bothers us there.
Mmh... I was thinking we could go by St. Dymphne's today. Just for a minute, before work.
Oh, Lucie... I know that voice.
It's just... what would you have said if Matron asked whether their seminary student could come practise on St. Dymphne's organ?
See. Exactly. That's what I said.
...Father Jean-Noël didn't tell the bishop it's dead?
I don't know. She just went on about how it'd be a sin to leave it sitting unused after all the work done on it this year. I... sort of lost the courage to ask after that.
Ohh, that miraculous restoration nobody seems to remember?
Oh, don't Babette me. You started it.

repeat.text: What lulls from a drawer and eases your blues, holds the colour of veins and a yesterday bruise?

answer.text: Ah, darling... It's Lavender Fleuries. Like those violet lavender sachets people keep in drawers to calm their nerves.

wrong_items.text: Mm. Nope. One more try, darling.

wrong_price.text: Hmm. That's not what it cost last time.

toooth.text: Oh Lord... dear, no. I almost took it without looking. You... you didn't mean to hand me that, right? Here... just take it back.

paying_lavenderless.text: Pity. We did have a little holy trinket for you.

paying.text: Correct, darling. See, Lucie, I knew we had a gift for riddles.
Lovely. Now then... which one do we give her?
Mm, maybe this one? No, wait. Hm...
Oh, this is hopeless. Pick a number, sweetheart. One to four.
{{card}}, then. Here, a prayer card for you. God bless and keep you.

checkout.text: So... I'll stop by Father Jean-Noël on my way. You can keep the packet, just give me one cigarette.
It's fine, I'll just borrow Father's lighter for a minute.
...Alright. Then I'll just head straight to the hospital.

entry.text: Good afternoon, {{name_yves}}. I need an ashtray for the workshop.
Accidentally retired the old one, and now customers are flicking ash into empty tobacco tins. Not great.

response.text: (Alright. Let's pull that thread.)
Couldn't it have been prevented? I heard bellows are often the first thing to go. Problematic part.
...Most irritating to check.
...Bellows are a pain, yeah. And in case of this particular organ, what was the point anyway?
The whole left half was a mess - pipes knocked out or missing, the case going soft with rot. Pedals warped and stiff. Keyboard too - half the keys loose, a few straight-up gone.
So... yeah. The bellows had plenty wrong with them, but they weren't what finished the organ. Whole thing was dying already.
And you helped it die faster?

Helped it die? I did every bloody check they asked for, filled out every repair request nice and proper, just how the diocese wants them. Told them it was falling apart and needed proper repairs, not patch jobs and prayers.
No reaction. Nothing changed.
Eventually I stopped checking it properly. Just looked at the parts you could see without crawling in all the way. Figured if they didn't care, why should I?

options.text: So you cracked first, like a loser?

response.text: ...Good Lord. And you had time to think before saying that.

options.text: Sounds like weak glutes to me

response.text: ...Good Lord. And you had time to think before saying that.
...Good Lord. And you had time to think before saying that.
*sigh*
Well. Maybe I could've done my job better.
...I'll take it off the repair cost. Not much, but fair's fair.
You can be really nasty, huh?
Restoration... Hm. Well, if you can count bringing a few dead stops back as restoration, then yes. I'll never forget that first chord that came out of it... Like it forgave us.
God, that was a while ago... Previous bishop was still around then, so... must be a good decade by now. Maybe a bit more.

After that... *sigh* it just sort of stalled. Paperwork went up. Silence came back down. Same thing when we asked them to send a stand-in organist while ours was away for a while. Nothing ever came of it.
Holding on, but it's getting tougher. Even booked extra sessions with Sister Priscilla.
The nun who stick needles in your...
Heavens, no. Still got all my teeth, and I intend to keep them. Just the ears.
That's right.
...What, to grow whiskers? No, no. The ears.
Cruel joke, {{name_yves}}. Didn't crawl back to it. Just an ashtray.
Cruel joke, {{name_yves}}. Didn't crawl back to it. Just an ashtray.

ears.text: If you're curious, she does nerves, hiccups and bad habits.

toooth.text: Oh, that's an interesting thing. You want me to take that tooth?

response.text: Alright then. If that's what you want.
Fair enough. Doesn't sound like the kind of matter I ought to carry around anyway.

checkout.text: Thanks. Ashes to ashes, tin to bin. Back to the organ for me.

Thinking I might take a couple days off after that. Me, the pub guy across the workshop, maybe even that suspicious bakery family, we're talking about building a proper resting spot for the seal on our street. Feels wrong, watching it lie there like it's waiting for someone to say it belongs.

Bet your block's planning one too. Pretty sure Félix already stocked up on materials, and your name's already on the volunteer list too. The man's always trying to domesticate anything that doesn't run off fast enough.
Okay, I should really go now. Take care, {{name_yves}}.

response.text: Ah. Right. Expectation is a vulgar little sin.
Mugwort Fleuries, child.
Very well. Mugwort Fleuries, please. I forgot one must now genuflect before the counter.

choose.text: I believe I have strength left for one more small trial. Choose it carefully.

diocese.text: Must be hard, relying on your own strength and a handful of local coins when something like the organ goes down. Aren't your higher-ups supposed to pay for things like restorations?
Oh, Abigaïl... Even the town hardly cared when it was alive. Why would the city?

I told them the poor thing had finally given up and asked for help, but as always, there were more important things. They always seem to know what St. Dymphne's needs... Better than the parish itself, I suppose.
But I'm sure Yves will coax it back into a voice soon, and on Sunday people will pretend they never doubted it.
We'll cope... somehow. We always do.

diocese_goBlunt.text: Enlighten me, Father. People above you seem to believe the organ was restored. Down here, the thing's sitting there broken. So what was it, a spiritual restoration?
...You stand here counting coins and rumours, catch a whisper or two, and suddenly you see through decades of parish life?
You think this place can survive on perfect paperwork and city approval?
You think we have the luxury of purity?!
Without me... this parish would've collapsed years ago.
The organ gutted for parts. People left to deal with their mess alone.
Maybe even someone's mother not getting a burial she couldn't afford?
But no. Please. Tell me how it should be done.

death.text: Did you read that thing about the organ in the paper? The way they described it - all those compartments, little hidden bits... Makes you think there's more going on in there than what you see from the pews.

And what is it you think is tucked away in there, hm? A staircase to Heaven? Perhaps a backup priest for emergencies, or even an entire second congregation nesting between the pipes? I insist, enlighten me.
It's an instrument of worship, not a story for children. Old, yes. Temperamental, certainly. But under proper supervision.
No one goes near it without my say-so. I am quite aware of what happens in MY church, I assure you.

death_goBlunt.text: Help me understand something, Father. That organ didn't just quietly give up on its own, did it? The bits I've heard suggest there was more... activity around it than you let on.
You people see one missing screw, and suddenly it's sabotage. Or possession. Or poor Raphaël wrestling pipes in the night. The town feeds on this nonsense.
What you need to understand is that gossip is not investigation. And parroting every stupid little theory that drifts past your counter is not your civic duty.
What happens in it, around it, inside it, is not some puzzle for you to pick at.
I will handle what needs handling. And you focus on your sacred duty of selling cigarettes.

seal.text: So what's the church's official position on the seal?
Of course. Out of everything, that is what we must discuss.
If Our Lord Himself walked through the square right now, half the town would step around Him to get a better look at the thing.
"Father, is it a sign?" "Father, why is it here?" "Father, should we move it? feed it? name it? baptise it?"
It is a wet creature that took a wrong turn and ended up here.

teeth.text: I'm helping Erika collect a few notes for an article about dental health in town. Habits, incidents, missing teeth... Anything interesting on your end?
Ah, at my age, each surviving tooth feels like a small miracle. You go... what, a year? two? without losing one, and you already start counting yourself lucky.
As for the parish... Church isn't exactly a theatre of smiles. Nor of bared fangs, thankfully. Looking at some parishioners I suspect they may have forgotten both expressions entirely.
So no, I'm afraid I have nothing scandalous for your article.

subtleEnd.text: ...Now forgive me for skipping to the part where you do your job, child.

toooth.text: Take it back. I've already got too many pieces of others.

entry.text: Evening! I've made a decision. Today is gonna be the day I become mysterious.

response.text: Not during my shift. I refuse to have this on my conscience.
(...Always hated being called her bad influence.)
Oh come on. Taking a moral stance? You?
Ugh. Fine. No pink cigarettes today.
Who am I to stop you.
(...They always called me her bad influence anyway.)
Perfect. Thank you.

options.text: Want to tell me something about that bloody note?

response.text: Oh. So you found that.
Umm...
Right, then... Guess that means you...
...Went digging in the rubbish.
...Took the bait and went picking through bin guts for a handful of damp paper... Filthy girl.
Sweet Christ, I'm so glad you did.
Shame it's too late for the ideal scenario, but... whatever. It left you with questions, didn't it?

options.text: People are setting up stuff for the seal?

response.text: Yes! Isn't it beautiful? Everyone's suddenly a carpenter now.

They're building little ramps and laying out old beach towels so it doesn't scratch its belly. Someone's planning a shaded nook with full interior decor and even a curtain, because apparently seals want privacy too.
Kiddie pools popping up here and there... It's like the whole town collectively lost its mind in the sweetest possible way.
We've even got polished city motors parked along the quay now. Amazing how quickly one discovers a deep, enduring love for marine wildlife.
Oh! And we're getting letters. You know, the usual "letters to the editor" sort, except they're addressed to the seal.
Definitely putting some of them in this Sunday's paper. Too good not to.

options.text: Smoking wrecks your teeth, you know

response.text: You start that, and your teeth will just drop out, Erika. Plink. Plink. Little white rain.
Yeah, yeah. Been hearing that speech since childhood.
Pencils, threads, wires, bottle caps, fishing lines, cracking nuts... Cigarettes would barely make the top ten worst things I've done to my teeth.
At this point we've reached an understanding. Whatever happens, happens.

options.text: Remind me what I'm selling you?

response.text: Fleuries. Pink ones. Look at my head if you forget.

options.text: Where did that paper come from?

response.text: Someone left it for me at the newsroom. No name, no return address, just that little treasure map and a bit of blood. Enough to get my attention.
Inside that left side? A whole damned labyrinth. Papers, notebooks, matchboxes, tins, weird little wrapped things - all crammed between pipes or pushed into cavities.
A stash? Some kind of postal system? God knows how long I was in there, elbows deep, trying to figure out what the hell the place even was.
And then - bang - something cracked me on the back of the head. Ears ringing. Floor tilting. Lights out.
Woke up on a pew with Father Jean-Noël rehearsing some sermon draft over me. For a second I thought that was it. Purgatory.

Later... When I finally got another chance to look, the notes, the parcels, the whole delicious mess were already gone. I pulled out half the pipes on that side trying to find even one scrap, but nothing.
Oh. Right. That. When I got knocked out, I'm pretty sure I saw the hem of an altar boy's surplice in the corner of my eye.
And, well... we've got one rather questionable altar boy who 1) has a history of hitting people, 2) is chronically allergic to me, but 3) used to eat sand pies with you.

...Honestly, after the stash evaporated and nothing else twitched for months, I just let the whole thing fade out of my brain. But then with everything bubbling again lately, I thought, hey, maybe the thread isn't dead after all.
Except now, without evidence or the one person I hoped to grill... I've got... nothing, really. No scenario left to act out.
Okay, look... I tried to put everything back how I found it... Ish. I mean, the thing still played at the next Mass, so I convinced myself it was fine.
In my defence, the place was already a mess. I thought if I nudged a few pipes out of place, it wouldn't matter. Like... what's one more crime in a crime scene?
...That's not great, isn't it?
*sigh*
Okay, I'll... sort something out. Make up for this little vandalism somehow.

end.text: Alright, prudence police, your shift's over, isn't it?

checkout.text: Thanks! Looks like closing time already?

start.text: *sigh* Now I sprint back the newsroom to fight with the typewriter and make the Sunday issue happen. But I've already picked the perfect spot for my grand debut as a smoker.

start_nocigs.text: *sigh* I'm heading back to the newsroom to enjoy deadline panic and all. But now you owe me some fun, and I've got an idea when.

wedding.text: My friends are getting married next Friday. Ridiculous couple, but the party's going to be good. Out in the moors, strange music, fog, mud... Might even cheer you up.
Come if you feel like it. I'd really like that.
Alright, off I go. Good night, Gail.
